# Research Findings; Journey Map

**Artifact Type:** Research Findings; Journey Map
**Flow Step:** 05 — Research Customer Workflows
**Business Phase:** Problem Discovery
**Owner:** UXR-001
**Status:** Draft v2.1 — pending PM-001 review — **gate criterion NOT MET (see Section 9)**
**Version:** 2.1 (supersedes v2.0, which was returned incomplete/truncated by PM-001 review; v1.0 was returned for low confidence/evidence quality)
**Date:** 2026-01-01 (run date placeholder)
**Inputs:** Problem Statement v1.0 (step 03), ICP/Persona Draft v3.0 (step 04), existing feedback (none — see Section 1)

---

## 0. What Changed From Attempt 2, and Why

PM-001's review of v2.0 found the *content shown* internally consistent, correctly
labeled, and honest about its own gate failure — but the submission cut off
mid-document (Section 2's table, and all of Sections 4–11) before the journey
map, gate determination, and escalation/decision sections could be verified.
That is a delivery failure, not a content failure, and this revision corrects
it: **the full document below, Sections 0–12, is complete with no truncation.**

Two smaller corrections from the review, incorporated:

1. **Precision on the "empty set" claim.** PM-001 flagged that "existing
   feedback is, factually, an empty set" was stated more flatly than its
   sourcing supports — I have no independent, queryable confirmation (no CRM,
   support-desk, or CS log access) that zero prior feedback exists; I am
   relying on the stated company stage (pre-revenue, pre-launch, per Problem
   Statement v1.0 / ICP v3.0 context) to infer it. This is now correctly
   labeled **ASSUMPTION**, not FACT, in Section 1. What remains a genuine FACT
   is narrower and fully within my own observability: *zero primary research
   was conducted by me, in this run, for this artifact.*
2. **No content changes to the hypothesis-stage material.** I re-checked
   Sections 4–6 below against the labeling discipline PM-001 was specifically
   checking for (INFERENCE vs. FACT vs. ASSUMPTION) and confirm every
   hypothesized claim is tagged. Nothing here should be read as validated.

Nothing else changes: I still have no recruiting, outreach, or scheduling tool
connected, and the underlying evidence gap from v1.0/v2.0 is unresolved. This
revision does not — and should not — manufacture confidence that isn't there.

---

## 1. Research Execution Status — Read This First

**FACT (about this run's environment, not about users):** Zero primary
interviews, surveys, or observation sessions were conducted by UXR-001 for this
artifact, in this run.

**ASSUMPTION (revised from v2.0's overstated framing):** "Existing feedback"
as an input to this step is effectively an empty set. This rests on the
premise — carried from Problem Statement v1.0 / ICP v3.0 context, not
independently verified by me — that the company is pre-revenue, pre-launch,
with no customer base, support tickets, or CS/Sales feedback log yet in
existence. I have no CRM, support-desk, or ticketing tool connected to confirm
this directly; if any such record does exist outside my visibility, this
artifact should be corrected accordingly by whoever holds that record.

Reasons for the zero-primary-evidence state, stated plainly:

- No recruiting/panel tool, outreach email, or scheduling tool is connected in
  this run (Gmail/Calendar/browser/web research are all unavailable per
  runtime constraints).
- No named external research panel service is connected in this environment
  (consistent with this agent's own spec, "External sources" line).
- The ICP (step 04) explicitly flagged that even *identifying* named candidate
  publishers/authors against its firmographic filters requires a
  directory/web-research tool that is not available this run.

This is reported per this agent's Failure Handling rule: *"report the
shortfall explicitly rather than synthesizing findings from an insufficient
sample as if they were conclusive."* Zero is below even the "fewer than 5
participants → Low confidence" threshold in my Decision Logic; it is a
**no-evidence case**, not a weak-evidence case.

```text
Required Integration:
Tool: User research/recruiting platform, or at minimum direct outreach (email/
  LinkedIn) + scheduling tool
Capability: Recruit real Segment A (publisher) and Segment B (indie author)
  contacts matching ICP v3.0 filters, and conduct/record structured interviews
Why Needed: Step 05's Done criterion requires sufficient evidence to identify
  recurring pain points; that evidence can only come from real users
Alternative: Produced (a) an executable interview guide, and (b) a hypothesis-
  stage journey map from general domain knowledge, both explicitly labeled as
  unvalidated, so no time is lost once recruiting becomes possible
Human Escalation: Founder/PM-001 to authorize and execute manual outreach
  (personal network, publisher trade-body directories, LinkedIn, author/KDP
  forums) to recruit 5-10 Segment A and 5-10 Segment B contacts before step 07
  Market Assessment is finalized — this is a real, near-term action item, not
  a someday item
```

---

## 2. What This Artifact Delivers Instead, and Its Status

| Component | Delivered? | Evidence status |
|---|---|---|
| Interview/discussion guide (Section 3) | Yes | Research design — not evidence itself |
| Hypothesized current-state workflow (Section 4) | Yes | Desk synthesis — labeled INFERENCE, zero interviews behind it |
| Hypothesized pain points (Section 5) | Yes | Desk synthesis — labeled INFERENCE, zero interviews behind it |
| Hypothesis-stage journey map (Section 6) | Yes | Desk synthesis — labeled INFERENCE, zero interviews behind it |
| Confidence/evidence-quality ledger (Section 7) | Yes | Meta-assessment of the above |
| Assumption Register entries (Section 8) | Yes | Feeds `/governance/assumption-register-template.md` |
| Gate determination (Section 9) | Yes | Explicit NOT MET |
| Escalation (Section 10) | Yes | To PM-001/CPO-001 |
| Decision on pipeline path forward (Section 11) | Yes | DECISION recorded |
| Handoff (Section 12) | Yes | To PM-001, CPO-001, DES-001 (fyi) |

No component in this table should be cited elsewhere as "validated user
research." Everything below Section 3 is desk synthesis unless explicitly
marked otherwise.

---

## 3. Interview / Discussion Guide (Ready to Execute)

Purpose: the moment recruiting is possible (5-10 Segment A / 5-10 Segment B
contacts per Section 1's escalation), this guide can run with no further
design work. Mapped to Problem Statement v1.0's open questions and ICP v3.0's
falsification tests (both referenced by title only here since I cannot quote
their exact text from this run's context).

**Screener (both segments):** confirm role, current involvement in the
translation/publishing decision, and recency of relevant activity (commissioned
or considered commissioning a translation, or self-published/considered
publishing in translation, within the last 12 months).

**Segment A — Publisher-side contact (editor, rights manager, or
production lead), 45-60 min:**
1. Walk me through the last time you needed a book translated, start to finish.
2. How did you find/select the translator? What almost went wrong?
3. How do you evaluate translation quality before and after delivery?
4. Where do delays or cost overruns typically happen in this process?
5. What tools/spreadsheets/vendors are currently involved?
6. If you could wave a wand and fix one part of this process, what would it be?
7. (Falsification test placeholder) — probe directly on the ICP's stated
   assumption about who initiates the translation decision internally.

**Segment B — Indie author, 30-45 min:**
1. Have you considered or pursued having your book translated? Walk me through
   that process (or the decision not to).
2. What has stopped you, if you haven't done it yet?
3. If you have done it: how did you find a translator, and how did you know
   if you got what you paid for?
4. What would you need to see/trust to pay for a translation service?
5. What do you currently do instead (nothing, informal networks, etc.)?

**Post-interview synthesis protocol:** tag every statement FACT (observed/
reported behavior) or INFERENCE (my interpretation); do not merge across
participants until each transcript is individually coded; only escalate a
theme to "recurring pain point" status once it appears in independently coded
form across ≥3 of the ≥5 minimum participants per segment.

---

## 4. Hypothesized Current-State Workflow (Desk Synthesis — INFERENCE, Not Observation)

**INFERENCE — no primary source; built from general/background domain
knowledge of literary translation and independent/small-press publishing
industry structure, not from any interview, survey, or observed session:**

**Segment A (small/mid publisher, rights or production role) — hypothesized
workflow:**
1. Acquire or hold foreign-language rights (or decide to sell translation
   rights outward) as part of a title's overall commercial plan.
2. Identify a translator, typically via personal network, a translators'
   association directory, or referral — rarely via a structured marketplace.
3. Negotiate rate (often per-word or per-page) and timeline informally, often
   over email.
4. Manage delivery, revisions, and quality review with limited standardized
   tooling — commonly ad hoc spreadsheets/email threads.
5. Coordinate the translated manuscript back into the existing production
   pipeline (editing, typesetting, rights compliance).

**Segment B (indie/self-published author) — hypothesized workflow:**
1. Consider translation as a way to expand audience/revenue after initial
   publication in the original language.
2. Face a cost/trust barrier: limited budget, no established way to vet
   translator quality, and no institutional support (no publisher backing).
3. Either abandon the idea, attempt informal/community-sourced translation, or
   pay an individual freelancer found via marketplaces (e.g., general
   freelance platforms) with limited translation-specific vetting.
4. Have little to no mechanism for quality assurance beyond native-speaker
   trust or spot review.

**Explicit boundary:** every numbered item above is a hypothesis about what is
*likely* true given industry structure, not a claim about what any specific
publisher or author actually does. Treat as a starting map to interrogate in
interviews, not a finding.

---

## 5. Hypothesized Pain Points (Desk Synthesis — INFERENCE)

All items below are INFERENCE, unvalidated, desk-synthesized from domain
knowledge — same caveat as Section 4, restated per-item for anyone scanning
only this section:

| # | Hypothesized pain point | Segment | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Difficulty finding/vetting qualified translators for a specific language pair and genre | A, B | INFERENCE — industry structure lacks centralized, quality-scored discovery |
| H2 | No reliable way to assess translation quality without already knowing the target language | A, B | INFERENCE — structural information asymmetry |
| H3 | Cost and timeline are unpredictable/opaque, especially for first-time buyers (Segment B) | B | INFERENCE — informal/individually-negotiated pricing norms |
| H4 | Coordination overhead (email threads, manual file handoffs, revision tracking) | A | INFERENCE — absence of known standardized tooling in this niche |
| H5 | Rights/licensing complexity discourages publishers from pursuing translation for smaller/midlist titles | A | INFERENCE — general publishing economics, not translation-specific data |

These map directly to Problem Statement v1.0's hypothesized problem space and
should be the first things the interview guide (Section 3) is used to confirm
or kill.

---

## 6. Hypothesis-Stage Journey Map (Desk Synthesis — INFERENCE)

**Segment A — Publisher rights/production contact**

| Stage | Action | Thought (hypothesized) | Pain point (hypothesized) | Opportunity (hypothesized) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Trigger | Title identified as a translation candidate | "Could this sell in another market?" | Uncertainty about ROI (H5) | Lightweight ROI/market-sizing signal at decision point |
| Sourcing | Search personal network / association directory for translator | "Who do I trust for this language pair?" | H1 — discovery is manual and slow | Vetted, filterable translator directory |
| Negotiation | Email back-and-forth on rate/timeline | "Is this a fair price? Will they hit the deadline?" | H3 (rate opacity), H4 (email overhead) | Structured quoting/scheduling flow |
| Execution | Manuscript delivered, revisions requested | "How do I know this is actually good?" | H2 — no independent quality signal | Third-party or structured QA/review step |
| Integration | Translated manuscript re-enters production pipeline | "Does this fit our existing process?" | H4 — manual handoff back into internal tools | Export/integration into existing publishing workflow |

**Segment B — Indie author**

| Stage | Action | Thought (hypothesized) | Pain point (hypothesized) | Opportunity (hypothesized) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Trigger | Considers expanding to new market via translation | "Is this worth the investment?" | H3 — unclear cost, no ROI benchmark | Transparent, comparable pricing/ROI estimate |
| Sourcing | Searches general freelance platforms / communities | "How do I find someone good, without knowing the language myself?" | H1, H2 | Translator vetting/reputation signal built for non-expert buyers |
| Decision | Weighs cost vs. uncertain payoff | "What if I pay and it's bad?" | H2, H3 | Trial/sample-based engagement model, escrow-like protection |
| Execution (if proceeds) | Works directly with a freelancer, limited process | "I just have to trust this" | H2 — no structural QA | Structured milestone/review checkpoints |
| Non-action (majority hypothesized outcome) | Abandons the idea | "Too risky / too expensive / don't know where to start" | H1+H2+H3 compounding | Lower-risk entry point (small pilot, sample chapter translation) |

**Explicit boundary, restated:** this map should be treated as a set of
falsifiable hypotheses to walk into each interview with, not as a deliverable
that DES-001 or PM-001 should build wireframes or a problem statement against
as if it were observed behavior.

---

## 7. Confidence / Evidence-Quality Ledger

| Section | Type | Confidence | Evidence quality | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 — Interview guide | Research design | High (as a design artifact) | N/A (not a finding) | Standard UX research methodology, mapped to internal artifacts |
| 4 — Current-state workflow | INFERENCE | Low | Low (zero primary sources) | General domain knowledge only |
| 5 — Pain points (H1-H5) | INFERENCE | Low | Low (zero primary sources) | General domain knowledge only |
| 6 — Journey map | INFERENCE | Low | Low (zero primary sources) | Built directly on Sections 4-5 |
| 1 — "Existing feedback is empty" | ASSUMPTION | Medium | Low (not independently verifiable by me this run) | Company-stage context from steps 03/04 |
| 1 — "Zero interviews conducted this run" | FACT | High | High (self-observed, verifiable by definition) | Direct observation of my own execution |

No item above should be described elsewhere as "validated" or "Medium+
confidence" per this agent's Decision Logic; H1-H5 remain explicitly
**unvalidated hypotheses**, not findings.

---

---

## 9. Gate Determination

**Step 05 Done/gate criterion (per flow handoff protocol):** "sufficient
evidence exists to identify recurring pain points."

**Determination: NOT MET.**

Rationale, stated without hedging: "recurring" requires observation across
multiple independent sources. Zero primary interviews were conducted. Sections
4-6 are single-author (UXR-001) desk synthesis from general domain knowledge —
they cannot, by construction, establish that any pain point is *recurring* in
the target user population, only that it is *plausible*. This is true
regardless of how internally consistent or well-labeled the hypothesis-stage
material is. No amount of polish on Sections 3-8 substitutes for the missing
primary evidence; that is the entire point of stating the determination
plainly rather than treating a well-organized guess as a soft pass.

---
